text.en: 1. This Order may be cited as the Immigration (Exemption from section 6) Order.

2. In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires —
“air service” means a service comprising the carriage of passengers or cargo for hire by means of an aircraft;
“airline crew member” means a person who is employed as a flight crew member by an international air carrier or other air service.
[S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]
[Deleted by S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]

3.—(1) The following classes of persons are exempt from section 6(1) of the Act:
(a)the classes of persons specified in the First Schedule, and their spouses and dependent children, not being permanent residents of Singapore; and
[S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]
(b)the classes of persons specified in the Second Schedule or Fourth Schedule.
[S 683/2026 wef 30/09/2026]
(2) The exemption conferred by this paragraph shall be subject to regulation 39 of the Immigration Regulations (Rg 1).

4. The following classes of persons are exempt from section 6(2) of the Act:
(a)the classes of persons specified in the First Schedule, and their spouses and dependent children;
(b)the classes of persons specified in the Third Schedule or Fourth Schedule; and
[S 683/2026 wef 30/09/2026]
(c)permanent residents of Singapore.
[S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]
5. The burden of proof that any person is a person to whom this Order applies shall lie upon that person.
6. Nothing in this Order shall be construed to exempt any person from examination under section 24, 25, 25A or 26 of the Act, as the case may be.

FIRST SCHEDULE
Paragraphs 3(1)(a) and 4(a)
1. Members of such visiting force as the Minister may determine.
2. Persons duly accredited as diplomatic or consular representatives to Singapore and any staff of such diplomatic or consular representatives who in the opinion of the Minister should be exempted from section 6(1) and (2) of the Act.
3. Persons upon whom the immunities and privileges referred to in Part 2 or 3 of the Second Schedule to the International Organisations (Immunities and Privileges) Act 1948 have been conferred under that Act.
[S 329/2025 wef 31/12/2021]
[G.N. Nos. S 648/2005; S 443/2008]

SECOND SCHEDULE
Paragraph 3(1)(b)
1. Any member of the Singapore Armed Forces travelling on duty.
2. Any non-citizen (but not a permanent resident of Singapore) airline crew member of an international air carrier or other air service who, in the course of a journey on duty from a place outside Singapore to Singapore, or from a place outside Singapore to a place outside Singapore —
(a)travels to Singapore in the course of his employment as a flight crew member on an aircraft of that international air carrier or other air service;
(b)is expected to leave Singapore in the course of his employment as a member of the flight crew of, or as a passenger on, such an aircraft within 30 days after arriving in Singapore; and
(c)enters Singapore at an authorised airport.
[S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]
3. Any head of state of a foreign country who is a guest of the Government.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]

THIRD SCHEDULE
Paragraph 4
1. Any head of state of a foreign country who is a guest of the Government.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]
2. Any non-citizen (but not a permanent resident of Singapore) airline crew member of an international air carrier or other air service referred to in item 2 of the Second Schedule who leaves Singapore from an authorised airport as a member of the flight crew of, or as a passenger on, an aircraft of an international air carrier or other air service within 30 days after arriving in Singapore.
[S 742/2025 wef 01/12/2025]
3. A non-citizen who —
(a)uses an automated clearance system for immigration clearance;
(b)obtains immigration clearance through the system whether by presenting a passport or other travel document to the system or by using other means (such as by presenting a personal identifier to the system or using a QR code generated from an electronic service specified by the Controller); and
(c)is not required by an immigration officer to appear before an immigration officer for immigration clearance after so using the automated clearance system.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]
4. Any holder of a dependant’s pass issued under regulation 11 of the Immigration Regulations (Rg 1).
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]
5. Any holder of a visit pass issued under regulation 12 of the Immigration Regulations that authorises the holder to remain in, or enter and remain in, Singapore for a continuous period of 90 days or more.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]
6. Any holder of a visit pass issued under regulation 12 of the Immigration Regulations that authorises the holder to enter Singapore on more than one occasion.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]
7. Any holder of a student’s pass issued under regulation 14 of the Immigration Regulations.
[S 329/2025 wef 30/05/2025]

FOURTH SCHEDULE
Paragraphs 3 and 4
Cross-border railways-related exemption
1.—(1) Any term in this Schedule that is defined in the Cross-Border Railways (Border Control Co‑location) Act 2026 has the meaning given to that term in that Act unless the term is otherwise defined in this Schedule.
(2) In this Schedule —
“cross-border railway” means a railway that —
(a)has a railway network with a terminus in Singapore and runs to any part of peninsular Malaysia; and
(b)is constructed under the Cross‑Border Railways Act 2018;
“defined route” means —
(a)travelling to Malaysia from Singapore —
(i)by rail via the Woodlands North Station at 1 Woodlands North Coast Road, Singapore 738979 to Bukit Chagar Station at Jalan Tengku Azizah, 80300 Johor Bahru, Johore Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia; or
(ii)by road or on foot via the Woodlands Checkpoint at 1200 Woodlands Road or the Woodlands Checkpoint at 21 Woodlands Crossing in Singapore to Bangunan Sultan Iskandar at Jalan Lingkaran Dalam, Bukit Chagar, 80300 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia; or
(b)travelling to Singapore from Malaysia —
(i)by rail via Bukit Chagar Station at Jalan Tengku Azizah, 80300 Johor Bahru, Johore Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia to the Woodlands North Station at 1 Woodlands North Coast Road, Singapore 738979; or
(ii)by road or on foot via Bangunan Sultan Iskandar at Jalan Lingkaran Dalam, Bukit Chagar, 80300 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia to the Woodlands Checkpoint at 1200 Woodlands Road or the Woodlands Checkpoint at 21 Woodlands Crossing in Singapore;
“Malaysia’s CIQ zone in Singapore” means the area demarcated under section 7(1) of the Cross-Border Railways (Border Control Co-location) Act 2026;
“technical assistance” includes troubleshooting, user assistance, system maintenance or cybersecurity services.
2. A Malaysian border protection service officer who travels to or from Singapore by a defined route for the purpose or in the course of his or her performing duties as —
(a)a Malaysian preclearance officer in Singapore in respect of a cross‑border railway;
(b)a Malaysian border protection service officer in peninsular Malaysia in respect of a cross‑border railway; or
(c)a Malaysian incident management officer in respect of a cross‑border railway affected by a railway occurrence necessitating incident management operations.
3. A non-citizen individual who —
(a)is, or is an employee of, a person contracted or engaged by the Government of Malaysia to provide technical assistance in hardware, software or network issues connected with border clearance or railway security checks by a Malaysian border protection service of people and goods travelling by any cross-border train using a cross-border railway;
(b)travels to or from Singapore by a defined route in connection with the individual providing, at the particular request of a Malaysian border protection service officer, any technical assistance mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) within Malaysia’s CIQ zone in Singapore;
(c)provides that technical assistance solely within Malaysia’s CIQ zone in Singapore; and
(d)is approved by the Minister to be at work in Malaysia’s CIQ zone in Singapore for the purpose in sub-paragraph (b).
[S 683/2026 wef 30/09/2026]
